Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the draft MSA and Order Form. Procurement and legal at Stellaris ran a redline and have one substantive ask that we want to elevate early: because our deployments include on-site device installs in clinical settings, our procurement template requires an explicit carve-out for personal injury and physical property damage caused by supplier activity.

Specifically we proposed language in Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) that would carve out claims for bodily injury, death, and tangible property damage from the cap on liability. We understand this is atypical for SaaS vendors, but for our regulator environment and patient-safety obligations this is a hard requirement.

I've attached our redlines (Stellaris_Redlines_20261205.docx). Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept this exception or propose a narrow alternative (cap level, insurer requirement, indemnity)? We're on a compressed timetable for procurement and would like to close next week if possible.

Thanks —

Hi Rachel / Emily —

Thanks — I reviewed the redline. A few quick points and a proposed path forward.

1) Baseline: Redwood's standard MSA treats all customer damages as subject to the mutual cap (typical SaaS position). We do not routinely accept unlimited carve-outs for bodily injury/property damage because our product is software-first and our operational risk profile is different than a manufacturer or installer.

2) When a customer requires an exception because of on-site activity or hardware the common compromises are:
   - A narrow carve-out that applies only to (a) bodily injury or death, and (b) physical damage to customer property, and only to the extent proximately caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct during on-site services or Redwood-supplied hardware; AND
   - A sensible cap for those limited claims (e.g., $5M–$10M) rather than removing the cap entirely; AND
   - Proof of insurance (commercial general liability and, if hardware/medical device exposure, appropriate limits) naming the customer as additional insured; AND
   - A reciprocal indemnity for third-party claims where appropriate.

3) Proposed redline snippet (for insertion into Limitation of Liability):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither party excludes liability for: (a) death or bodily injury caused by that party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; or (b) direct physical damage to tangible property proximately caused by a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct during on-site services or in connection with equipment provided by such party. For claims described in clause (b) above, the parties agree that liability shall be capped in the aggregate at Five Million United States Dollars (USD $5,000,000). Such cap is in lieu of any claim for consequential or punitive damages for the same event."

4) Conditions to accept:
   - Redwood requires a certificate of insurance showing at least $5M CGL and umbrella/exec-level excess limits, naming Stellaris as an additional insured for claims arising from Redwood's on-site activities;
   - A customary indemnity provision for third-party claims tied to Redwood's acts/omissions;
   - A mutual escalation: if Stellaris insists on removing the cap entirely we will need a commercial exception approved by senior leadership and underwrite by our insurance broker.

I've attached a tracked redline for the MSA that illustrates the insertion (Redlined_MSA_20261206.docx). If Stellaris can accept a $5M cap + insurance + indemnity, we believe that's a principled compromise that addresses patient-safety concerns while keeping reasonable commercial limits for Redwood.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Redlined_MSA_20261206.docx

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@stellarishealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 14:33:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines (personal injury/property damage carve-out)

Laura — thank you for the thoughtful response. A few clarifications from our side:

- Stellaris cannot accept a $0 cap for personal injury risks — we proposed removing the cap for those categories because our legal, facilities and clinical risk teams need to preserve remedies for patient harm.
- If Redwood is willing to meet us in the middle, procurement is authorized to accept a monetary cap but it must be materially above $5M. Our risk team has suggested $25M for physical injury/property damage tied to clinical deployments.
- We can provide certificates of insurance and are open to the additional-insured requirement, but the higher cap is non-negotiable for internal sign-off unless Redwood offers a stronger indemnity (e.g., broader vendor indemnity for patient claims) or a different commercial offset (pricing/credits).

For context: Stellaris will be deploying Redwood-managed compute appliances in 20+ clinics under this order; the exposure is not solely configuration support. Our legal team will circulate a short risk summary (attached).

—Emily
Emily Chen
Sr. Counsel, Stellaris Health
Attachment: Stellaris_Risk_Statement.pdf

Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines (personal injury/property damage carve-out) — proposed compromise and next steps

Emily / Rachel — thanks for the speedy engagement and for the context around on-prem appliances. I pulled together a proposed middle ground after conferring with Legal and our commercial leadership.

Summary of Redwood's compromise proposal:
1) Narrow carve-out: Redwood will agree to a limited carve-out from the liability cap that applies only to: (i) death or bodily injury, and (ii) direct physical damage to tangible property, where such harm is proximately caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct arising from (A) Redwood-provided hardware or (B) on-site services performed by Redwood personnel.
2) Cap: Redwood proposes a capped liability for these categories at Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (USD $7,500,000) in the aggregate per contract.
3) Conditions: acceptance of this carve-out is conditioned on: (a) Stellaris providing a certificate of insurance showing Commercial General Liability and umbrella/excess limits consistent with the cap and naming Redwood as additional insured where appropriate; (b) a reciprocal indemnity for third-party claims related to customer-supplied equipment or acts; (c) a standard notice-and-cooperation clause and reasonable mitigation obligations; and (d) final executive sign-off (commercial exception) to be obtained within two business days of agreement on language.
4) Alternative: If Stellaris cannot accept the $7.5M cap, we are prepared to increase to $10M subject to (i) an incremental commercial concession (e.g., term commitment or price adjustment) and (ii) underwriter sign-off.

Next steps: 
- If this captures the direction Stellaris needs, can you confirm acceptance of the $7.5M cap + insurance + indemnity by EOD Wednesday 12/9?
- If Stellaris must insist on $25M, we will need an expedited executive-level exception and insurance underwriting review; please advise and we'll tee up our CRO/GC for a short call.
